title: Reference-image conditioning for etch diagrams
summary: Let etch reuse an approved draft image as a visual reference for the next generation, so a diagram's composition and style carry over instead of being re-rolled from scratch. This gives etch a real draft-to-final workflow, working around the image models' lack of a reproducibility seed.
motivation: Nano Banana / Gemini image models are autoregressive with no seed, so the only way to keep a composition across generations is to pass the prior image back in as a reference.

included: etch.py provider seam (ImageProvider.generate) and provider capability model
etch.py GeminiProvider request construction (image Parts) and MAIProvider capability rejection
etch.py tool boundary: reference-image load/validate/encode + start_diagram_job + _run_generation threading
excluded: Web frontend UI to pick, upload, or preview a reference image (web/frontend/**)
Browser file-upload / data-URL transport — the web API accepts server-accessible file paths in V1, mirroring the MCP tool
Reference conditioning on MAI-Image-2.5 — declared unsupported in V1 (its Foundry endpoint is text-to-image only; OpenRouter image-edit behavior for MAI is unverified)
Any change to the no-reference code path's output or request shape (must stay byte-identical)

design_facts.stack: Python MCP server (FastMCP) + FastAPI web backend; google-genai SDK for Gemini, httpx for MAI-Image-2.5; pytest, run via uv

work_items.title: Accept reference images in the provider layer
work_items.summary: Teach the image-provider seam to take optional reference images, wire them into the Gemini request, and read/validate/encode them from disk at the tool boundary — with the no-reference path left byte-for-byte unchanged.

contract.exposes: ImageProvider.generate(prompt, aspect_ratio, resolution, api_key, reference_images=()) -> bytes, where reference_images is a sequence of neutral (image_bytes: bytes, mime_type: str) pairs; an empty sequence produces a request byte-identical to today's text-only path. Providers declare capability via max_reference_images (GeminiProvider = 14, MAIProvider = 0). GeminiProvider.generate appends image Parts (types.Part.from_bytes(data, mime_type)) to the single user Content when references are present, and builds contents identical to today when empty. MAIProvider.generate raises GenerationError when any reference image is supplied and is unchanged when none. A tool-boundary helper _load_reference_images(paths, provider) -> list[(bytes, mime)] reads each path and raises ValueError on a missing/unreadable file, an unsupported format (allowed: PNG/JPEG/WebP/HEIC), a count exceeding provider.max_reference_images, a provider whose max is 0, or a file over the per-file byte cap.

signals: contract-mutation: changes the ImageProvider.generate() seam signature (additive — new arg defaults to empty)
capability-escalation: new disk file IO and image decode at the tool boundary
blast-radius: etch.py is edited by two work items (ref-core and mcp-tool)

assertions: With reference_images empty, GeminiProvider builds the request contents byte-identical to the current text-only baseline (existing no-reference tests still pass).
With N reference images, GeminiProvider's request contents include N image parts alongside the text part (captured via a mocked genai client).
MAIProvider.generate raises when any reference image is supplied, and is unchanged (existing MAI transport tests pass) when none is.
_load_reference_images raises a clear ValueError for each of: missing file, unsupported format, count over the provider max, a provider with max 0 (MAI), and an oversized file.

work_items.title: Add a reference-image option to the diagram tool
work_items.summary: Give start_diagram_job an optional list of reference-image paths and pass them through the job runner to the provider, validating them up front so bad input fails before a job is queued.

contract.consumes: ref-core's _load_reference_images(paths, provider) and the generate(..., reference_images=...) seam.
contract.exposes: start_diagram_job(..., reference_images: Optional[list[str]] = None) — an optional list of image file paths on disk (typically a prior job's output PNG). When None or empty the call is byte-identical to today: _run_generation and provider.generate receive empty references. When provided, the paths are validated and encoded via _load_reference_images at the tool layer (fail-fast, before the job is queued, consistent with existing capability/audience validation), then threaded through _run_generation(..., reference_images=...) into provider.generate. _run_generation gains a reference_images parameter passed straight to provider.generate. The tool docstring documents the parameter, the draft-to-final workflow, and that MAI rejects references.

signals: contract-mutation: adds a public MCP tool argument (reference_images) to start_diagram_job (additive — optional, defaults to None)
blast-radius: etch.py is edited by two work items (ref-core and mcp-tool)

assertions: A default call (reference_images=None) invokes provider.generate with empty references — the call shape is byte-identical to today (verified with a mocked provider capturing args).
Passing file paths threads the decoded references through _run_generation into provider.generate (count and content match the inputs).
Supplying references for a provider that does not support them (MAI) raises ValueError before the job is queued — no worker thread is started and no job_id is returned.

work_items.title: Thread reference images through the web API
work_items.summary: Add an optional reference-image field to the web backend's job request and pass it into the shared generator, leaving the existing no-reference and mock-mode behavior unchanged.

contract.consumes: etch._run_generation(..., reference_images=...) from mcp-tool and the provider seam from ref-core.
contract.exposes: DiagramRequest.reference_images: Optional[list[str]] = None — an additive optional field on the POST /api/jobs body carrying server-accessible image file paths. execute_generation_task threads it into etch._run_generation(..., reference_images=...). When the field is absent, behavior is byte-identical to today, including the mock-mode fallback used when the selected provider has no key. Browser upload transport and any frontend UI are out of scope.

signals: contract-mutation: adds a field to the POST /api/jobs request body schema (DiagramRequest) (additive — optional, defaults to None)

assertions: POST /api/jobs with reference_images threads the paths into etch._run_generation (patched to capture the argument).
A request without the field behaves exactly as today, and the mock-mode path (no key configured) is unaffected.

work_items.title: Document the draft-to-final workflow
work_items.summary: Update the README, how-it-works, env example, and skill so users know how reference conditioning works, which providers support it, and why it exists.
work_items.contract: Update README.md (start_diagram_job signature with reference_images; a Models-table note that Gemini supports up to 14 references and MAI supports none; a new 'Iterative refinement (draft to final)' section explaining that these models have no reproducibility seed and that passing an approved draft back as a reference is how composition/style is preserved), how-it-works.md (mention reference conditioning in the provider-abstraction description), .env.example (note that reference conditioning needs no new env var), and skills/etch/SKILL.md (guidance on when to feed a prior diagram back as a reference). Prose must match the behavior shipped by ref-core, mcp-tool, and web-backend.

oracle.reason: Docs-only prose change; the repo configures no docs linter, link-checker, or CI doc gate (indeed no lint/typecheck tooling at all), so there is no CI-facing check to run. Accuracy is verified by review against the code shipped in the preceding items.
